Below is a 3-week peaking/taper plan for a 28‑year‑old female, intermediate recreational lifter preparing for a powerlifting meet in 21 days. This assumes the client has completed 12 weeks of accumulation and is currently handling near‑meet intensities (70–95%+ of single‑rep maxes) with good technical consistency. The goal: reduce overall training volume and maintain heavy/intensity exposure to preserve neuromuscular readiness, sharpen technique, and arrive fresh on meet day. Program is written assuming the meet will be on Day 21 (end of Week 3). Adjust the calendar so Meet Day = final planned session.

General principles used
- Taper volume progressively each week while retaining some heavy singles/doubles at or near openers and planned attempts to preserve specificity.
- Maintain bar speed and technique with submaximal dynamic work early in sets.
- Reduce accessory volume and total sets; keep assistance light/moderate and specific.
- Last heavy day (Week 2 lower) contains very limited top work; Week 3 is nervous-system tune and very low volume.
- Include recovery priorities: sleep, carbohydrate timing around sessions, hydration, and light mobility. Use deloading modalities (contrast showers, light massage/rolling) as tolerated.
- Warmups: general 5–10 min aerobic, mobility, dynamic prep, progressive sets to top working weight. Rest between heavy singles: 3–6+ minutes as needed.
- All percentages are of current training maxs or best recent competition-style lifts. If you prefer using projected meet attempts instead, set top singles relative to planned openers and projected second/third attempts.

Structure overview (3 training days/week; you can shift days but keep spacing such that final heavy exposure is 5–7 days before meet):
- Week 1 (Days 1–7): High intensity preserved, reduced volume ~60% of accumulation.
- Week 2 (Days 8–14): Intensity near meet attempts for singles/doubles, volume ~35–45%.
- Week 3 (Days 15–21): Taper/sharpen — very low volume, singles only at opener-level or slightly above for confidence; active recovery days. Meet Day on Day 21.

Suggested training-day layout (example order): Squat day, Bench day, Deadlift day. You may alternate order depending on priority/personal recovery.

Week 1 — Peaking Week A (moderate taper)
Goal: Keep heavy exposure; reduce assistance volume. Start focusing on exact set-up and commands used in meet.

Day 1 — Squat focus (moderate heavy)
- Warmup: 8–10 min bike + mobility and progressive bar work.
- Work sets:
  1. Back Squat: 1×5@60% (warm), 1×3@70%, 1×2@80%, 2×1@88–92% (singles, treat like heavy singles; last single possibly an opener/second attempt intensity). Rest 3–5 min between singles.
- Paused/topset: 2×2 paused squats @65% — technique.
- Assistance (reduced): Romanian Deadlifts 3×6 @60% of RDL best; Goblet/Front squat 2×8 for positioning; Core: 3×15 Pallof presses or deadbugs.
- Mobility & recovery: 10 min focused hip flexor/ankle mobility; foam rolling quads/glutes.

Day 3 — Bench focus (moderate heavy)
- Warmup: arm circles, band work, 5–8 min light cardio.
- Work sets:
  1. Bench Press: 1×5@60%, 1×3@72%, 1×2@80%, 2×1@90–93% (singles). Use competition pause and commands if possible.
- Paused/repetition work: 2×3 paused bench @70% for groove.
- Assistance: Close-grip bench 3×6 moderate weight; Dumbbell rows 3×8 each side; Triceps pushdowns 3×12 light–moderate.
- Scapular/shoulder mobility and posterior chain activation.

Day 5 — Deadlift focus (moderate heavy)
- Warmup: 8–10 min bike + mobility; progressive deadlift warmups.
- Work sets:
  1. Conventional/Sumo Deadlift: 1×5@60%, 1×3@72%, 1×2@82%, 2×1@90–92% (singles). Focus on set-up, tightness, and lockout.
- Technique: 2×3 rack pulls just below knee @70% for confidence in lockout (light).
- Assistance: Bulgarian split squats 2×8 each leg; Hamstring curl 3×10 light; Core: 3×12 heavy carries (farmer carry) for 30–50 m.
- Recovery: mobility and glute activation.

Notes for Week 1
- Keep RPE of heavy singles around 8–9 (not max out to failure). If a single is very taxing, reduce the second to a lighter top single that session.
- Volume cut relative to accumulation: fewer backoff sets and fewer assistance sets.

Week 2 — Peaking Week B (sharpening)
Goal: Hit weights near planned meet attempts once, reduce volume further and preserve neural readiness.

Day 8 — Squat heavy but short
- Warmup and technique work.
- Work sets:
  1. Back Squat: 1×3@60% warm, 1×1@85% (simulated opener or second), 1×1@92–95% (planned second/third attempt or heavy single). Only 2 top singles for the day. Rest 4–6 min.
- Light backoff: 1×3 @70% for speed and groove.
- Assistance: Hip thrusts 2×8 light; ab wheel/anti-extension 2×10.
- Recovery modality: contrast showers or light massage if available.

Day 10 — Bench heavy but short
- Warmup.
- Work sets:
  1. Bench Press: 1×3@60%, 1×1@85% (opener), 1×1@92–95% (second/third attempt simulation if needed). Use competition pause, count commands.
- Light backoff: 1×3@70%.
- Assistance: Light rows 2×8, face pulls 3×12, triceps 2×10.
- Note: If bench is not a priority, drop the 92–95% single to keep freshness.

Day 12 — Deadlift heavy but short
- Warmup.
- Work sets:
  1. Deadlift: 1×3@60%, 1×1@85%, 1×1@92–96% (near planned second/third attempt). Keep single technical and not maximal failure.
- Light backoff: 1×3@70% or a couple of speed triples at ~60–65% if safer for the hips/lower back.
- Assistance: Light glute ham raises 2×6, reverse hypers 2×10.
- End with mobility and light walking to relieve stiffness.

Notes for Week 2
- This week contains your last heavy/top singles. Keep total training time short; limit accessory volume to 20–30 minutes.
- If any lift feels off or extremely heavy, drop the top single and substitute with a confidence opener (85–90%) only.
- Remove anything that causes unusual soreness or leaves the client flat.

Week 3 — Meet Week (taper & sharpen)
Goal: Full recovery and nervous system readiness; brief, low volume, technical reminders. No true max attempts. Meet day is Day 21.

Day 15 (7 days out) — Light full-body session (technical)
- Warmup.
- Squat: 1×2@60% (or 2×1 at opener weight for groove); focus on depth/commands; no grinding.
- Bench: 1×2@60% (or 2×1 at opener weight) with paused reps.
- Deadlift: 1×1–2 at 60–70% — keep submaximal and technique-focused.
- Mobility and activation; keep session under 45 minutes.
- Sleep, carb load moderately evening prior (not necessary to spike body weight).

Day 18 (4 days out) — Very light nervous system tune (optional)
- Short session: Warmup, then 1–2 singles at opener weights for each lift if desired, but many lifters skip heavy work this close.
- Or perform short mobility session and light band pull‑aparts, scapular work, and some walking. Session 20–30 minutes max.
- Focus on hydration and full meals; carbs as usual.

Day 20 (1 day out) — Pre-meet activation (optional)
- Very short activation session: bodyweight squats, bench touch-and-go with light bar, 1 light deadlift movement pattern (just hip hinge), plus mobility and visualization. Keep it <20 min.
- Pack gear, review attempt strategy, and sleep well.

Short answer: keep the cue, but avoid heavy new technical changes in the last 3 weeks. Use low-volume, high-specificity groove work (light paused reps, touch-and-go reps at opener-level, banded/bench-press-specific isometrics) to reinforce the shoulder-pack cue without risking fatigue or disruption.

Explanation and practical plan

1) Why keep the cue (but don’t overhaul)
- A cue to "pull the shoulders together" (pack the scapulae/retract the scapulae) is a stability and technique cue that generally improves shoulder position, bar path, and leg drive — and it’s safe to reinforce before a meet.
- Big technical changes late in a peaking block can cause confusion, timing issues, or a temporary performance drop. You don’t want the athlete experimenting with radically different timing or range-of-motion adjustments with heavy weights in the last 21 days.
- However, reinforcing an existing cue that she already uses and that feels natural is beneficial for consistency and confidence on meet day.

2) How to reinforce the cue safely during the 3-week peak
- Use very low-volume, high-specificity drills that emphasize the shoulder-pack without adding fatigue. Keep intensity conservative and keep reps low.
- Priority sessions: include in light technical days and warmups — not as a heavy new training focus.

Practical drills to include (use in warmups, paused work, and short technique sets)
- Band-assisted scapular retractions: 2×10–15 very light band pulls while standing or lying prone. Purpose: neurological reminder of scapular retraction without load.
- Bench press pauses with focus on pack: 1–2 sets of 2–3 paused reps at 60–70% (or opener-level during Week 3), exaggerated focus on pulling shoulders together and maintaining that shape through the pause. Keep these submaximal and short.
- Isometric holds at chest: 2–3 sets of 3–5 second isometric hold with 50–60% of the bar (or an unloaded bar) at the chest while squeezing shoulder blades. Very low volume.
- Touch-and-go opener singles with cue: on Week 2 when you take opener singles, have her focus on the cue and keep singles low in number (1–2) so the groove is practiced under load without volume.
- Floor/bench T-spine/shoulder mobility 2–3 minutes pre-lift: foam roll thoracic spine and do 6–8 band pull-aparts to reinforce the position before bar work.

Where to place these in the peaking plan
- Week 1: Add band scapular drills and 1 paused set (2 reps) in warmup on bench day. Keep assistance unchanged otherwise.
- Week 2: On bench top-single day, use 1–2 paused reps at 70% focusing on cue during warmup sets; take opener single(s) with the cue. Do 1 short band drill after the session for reinforcement.
- Week 3: Use only light reminder work — 1–2 opener-weight singles (or sub-opener at 60–70% if preferred) with strong emphasis on the cue during the warmup. No new heavy paused sets or technique overloads.

Coaching notes and monitoring
- Use short video recordings of a warmup single in Week 2 to confirm the shoulder position and make tiny micro-cues (e.g., "squeeze together, chest up, drive through feet") rather than introducing new large cues.
- If the athlete reports any shoulder pain when purposefully retracting more, regress to lighter banded work and consult a physio. Do not force a new position into heavy attempts.
- Keep verbal cues consistent and simple — the fewer the cues at meet time, the better. If "pull shoulders together" is what she already uses, stick to that phrasing.

Bottom line
- Do not abandon the cue — it’s useful and should be reinforced.
- Do not make large technical changes or add heavy volume focused on mechanics in the last 3 weeks.
- Reinforce the cue with short, low-volume drills, paused light reps, and opener singles with focus in Week 2; in Week 3 use only light reminders. This preserves specificity, reinforces motor patterning, and keeps her fresh for the meet.

Below is a practical, timed meet‑morning plan you can give your client. It assumes a typical local meet where the lifting session is in the morning-to-midday and she’s in a flight with the usual warmup room and platform sequence. Adjust exact clock times to the meet schedule (we’ll call “T” the platform start time for her flight).

General principles
- Eat and hydrate early enough to digest but close enough to have energy for the warmup room.
- Start with low‑level activation, progress through specific warmups, and finish with platform warmups timed to when she’ll be called.
- Keep things predictable: use the same pre‑lift warmup and cueing she practiced in the 3‑week peak.
- Stay relaxed and conserve energy between warmups — sitting, light mobility, and visualization are good.
- Communicate opener/attempt plan with coach/handler in advance so no last‑minute guessing.

Sample timeline (if platform session starts at T = 10:00)
- 06:00–07:00 — Wake up
  - Aim for a consistent wake time 2.5–4 hours before platform attempts begin so digestion and bathroom needs settle.
  - Gentle mobility in bed: 2–3 minutes of spinal rotations, ankle/hip circles.
  - Drink ~300–500 ml water on waking.

- 07:00 — Breakfast (2.5–3 hours before T)
  - Moderate-sized, familiar meal to top off glycogen: e.g., oats with banana and whey/Greek yogurt; or rice, eggs, avocado. Aim for 40–60 g carbs, 20–30 g protein, a little fat.
  - Avoid new foods or anything that usually causes GI upset.
  - Continue sipping water. If client uses caffeine, take a small dose now if that’s her usual habit (or save main dose for pre-warmup depending on tolerance).

- 08:30 — Light movement and final get-ready (1.5–1 hour before T)
  - Light 10–15 min gentle cardio (brisk walk or easy bike) only if she didn’t do any pre-meet cardio elsewhere. This is optional and should be very easy; it’s to raise body temperature.
  - Mobility: 5–8 min focused on thoracic spine, shoulders, hips, and ankle mobility. Keep it calm and short.
  - Start packing warmup gear: singlet, belt, wrist wraps, shoes, water, snacks (rice cakes, banana), tape, hand warmers if cold.

- 09:00 — Head to venue / check-in (1 hour before T)
  - Arrive early to check weigh-in status, equipment, and meet paperwork if needed.
  - Continue sipping fluids (aim for another 300–400 ml over the next hour).
  - Light snack if wanted (rice cake, banana, small yogurt) ~60–90 minutes before planned warmups.

- 09:30 — Begin bench/squat warmup sequence in warmup room (30 min before T)
  - Exact sequence will depend on flight order. Many meets call flights 30–45 min prior; be ready to start specific barbell warmups ~25–30 min before you’ll be called to platform.
  - General warmup (5–8 min): jog in place, arm circles, band pull‑aparts, scapular activation focusing on her “pull shoulders together” cue.
  - Mobility: 2–3 min dynamic movements specific to first lift (usually squat or bench depending on flight order).
  - Barbell warmups: progressively load and do 2–3 reps at each step up to opener weight. Warmup progression example for squat (adjust weights to percentages):
    - Empty bar x5–8
    - 40% x3
    - 60% x2
    - 75% x1–2
    - 85% x1 (confidence single)
    - Opener single @ planned opener
  - Emphasize technical cueing during each rep; keep pauses between warmup sets short but long enough to recover (1–3 min).
  - If bench is the first lift, use similar layout but include paused reps and shoulder-pack cueing.

- 09:50–10:00 — Final readiness before platform (10–0 min before T)
  - Finish last warmup single 3–6 minutes before being called to platform for opener.
  - Drink a last small amount (50–150 ml) and have a small simple carb (half a banana, few bites of a rice cake) if needed for confidence/energy.
  - Quick breathing/visualization: 1–2 minutes visualizing a successful attempt with cues (set-up, breathing, drive).
  - Put on singlet/belt/wraps and be at the call area 1–2 minutes before they call her to platform.

Platform protocol & timing (when called)
- When called to platform for opener, arrive promptly and take the bar if using the venue’s warmup area or use platform warmups if permitted.
- Keep rest between final warmup single and platform opener at least 3 minutes; if longer wait occurs, re-activate with 1–2 light barbell taps (just setup and unrack) or a short set of breath work and band pull-aparts to maintain readiness.
- If there is an unexpected delay >8–10 minutes, communicate with coach and consider repeating a 1–2 rep warmup with the empty bar or 40–60% to maintain body temperature, but don’t overdo it.

Between attempts
- Rest and refuel: eat a small carb snack (rice cake, banana, handful of gummy carbs) and sip water.
- Recovery breaths, mobility of the upper/lower body for 2–3 minutes to avoid stiffness.
- For second and third attempts, repeat a shortened warmup progression targeting that weight: quick jumps from 60→75→85→attempt (depending on time). Keep last heavy warmup singles 3–5 minutes before the attempt.
- Maintain consistent cueing: “pull shoulders together” for bench, specific squat and deadlift setup cues practiced during the peaking block.

Caffeine and stimulant timing
- If client uses caffeine, take a planned dose about 45–75 minutes before her first attempt (timing depends on individual response and dose). If she already had some in the morning, adjust to avoid over‑stimulation. Test routines in training — do not try new dosing on meet day.

Hydration and sodium
- Maintain consistent hydration the morning of; if in a cold venue and sweating less, don’t over-drink.
- If the client has to make a weight class and has completed rehydration, include a small salty snack (cracker with salt, broth) to manage electrolytes after weigh-in.

Troubleshooting common meet-day issues
- Feeling cold between warmups: use layers and hand/foot warmers, light movement (walk), and do a quick band activation circuit.
- Waiting too long for platform call: keep layers on, sip water, do short mobility circuits every 8–10 minutes; when 5–8 min out, do a short warmup single.
- Nervous GI: pre-plan bathroom breaks and keep snacks bland and tried-and-true.

Coach checklist to prep client beforehand
- Confirm flight time and call order; know how long warmup room queues usually are at that specific meet.
- Confirm opener/second/third attempt weights and have an alternate plan if an attempt is missed or judged No Lift.
- Ensure all equipment is competition legal and packed (singlet, belt, wraps, shoes, wrist wraps, socks for deadlift, tape, chalk).
- Bring a printed or app-based attempt tracker and a small bag of preferred snacks.

Example brief script/phrases to use with the lifter before an attempt
- “Set your feet, chest up, pull shoulders together, breath, drive.” (Short and consistent.)
- “One breath, lock the back, push.” Use the exact phrasing she practiced.

Week 1 — Peaking Week A (Days 1–7) — same as before but be conservative

Deload Week — Active recovery & neural refresh (Days 8–13 — 5–6 days)
Goal: remove accumulated fatigue, restore energy, preserve movement rehearsal without heavy load. This is NOT a technical overhaul week — keep cues light and familiar.

General deload rules
- Reduce training volume to ~30–40% of normal; intensity to ~50–60% of recent loads. Keep RPE low (<6).
- Session duration: 30–40 minutes maximum.
- No heavy singles >70–75%. Avoid multiple sets close to failure.
- Keep bench cue drills (shoulder-pack) as light band work and very short paused reps only.
- Include circulation-focused cardio sessions (12–20 min easy) 2–3 times across the deload week.
- Prioritize sleep, mobility, massage, and nutrition at maintenance.

Day D1 — Light technical lower
- Back Squat: empty bar x8, 40% x5, 55% x3 (all paused focus on setup). No heavy singles.

- Core/anti-extension: 2×10.
- 12–15 min easy bike.

Day D3 — Light technical upper
- Bench press: empty bar x8 (focus shoulder-pack), 40% x5 paused, 55% x3 touch-and-go. Keep reps crisp.

- Optional short swim or pool session (10–15 min).

Optional micro-sessions
- Two additional 10–15 min easy cardio sessions (walks, easy bike) spaced between lifting days. Keep intensity conversational.

Short Sharp Week — Condensed Heavy (Days 14–17)
Goal: provide the last heavy, neural stimulus while keeping volume very low so recovery before the meet is maximized. Heavy exposures should be targeted and short.

Structure
- 3 short sessions with 1–2 heavy singles per lift; these are the last heavy singles before the meet and should occur ~7–10 days out from the meet depending on how you schedule.
- Keep assistance minimal (1–2 light exercises for movement pattern maintenance).

Day S1 — Squat top singles
- Warmup: mobility + progressive bar work.
- Back Squat: 1×3@60% warm; 1×1@85% (opener simulation); 1×1@92–95% (if feeling good; otherwise stop at opener). Only 1–2 top singles.
- Light accessory: 2×6 hip thrusts, 2×10 ab work.
- Finish with 10–12 min easy bike if needed.

Day S2 — Bench top singles (48–72 hours after squats)

- Bench: 1×3@60%, 1×1@85% (opener), optional 1×1@92–95% depending on readiness. Use paused reps in warmup.

Day S3 — Deadlift top singles (48–72 hours after bench)
- Warmup and deadlift progressive sets.
- Deadlift: 1×3@60%, 1×1@85%, optional 1×1@92–96% as feel allows. Keep it conservative if any residual fatigue.

Meet Week — Taper & Meet (Days 18–21)

- Be conservative with the final heavy singles in Short Sharp Week. The purpose is neural priming and confidence — not to PR in training.

Adjust portions to her bodyweight and usual intake — the guidance below is for a ~60–75 kg intermediate female lifter; scale portions up/down for larger or smaller athletes.

Goals
- Top up muscle glycogen without causing GI distress or large swings in bodyweight.
- Ensure optimal hydration and sodium/electrolyte balance so she’s not sluggish or cramping.
- Maintain familiar foods and timing — do not introduce anything new.

General macro targets (48→24 hours before)
- Calories: at or slightly above maintenance (no need for large surplus).
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day (spread across meals) — supports recovery.
- Fat: moderate but not excessive at main meals (keep meals easy to digest).
- Carbohydrates: increase moderately to top up muscle glycogen.

Carbohydrate targets
- 48–24 hours before meet (Day –2 and Day –1): aim for ~4–6 g/kg/day total carbs.
  - For a 65 kg lifter that’s ~260–390 g carbs/day.
  - This level increases muscle glycogen without extreme water loading.
- The day of the meet (Day 0 pre-lift): have 1–3 g/kg in the 3–4 hours before lifting (depending on tolerance) and small 15–30 g carbohydrate snacks between attempts as needed.

Fluids & sodium
- Fluids: aim for ~30–40 ml/kg/day as baseline (about 1.8–2.6 L/day for 60–65 kg) plus extra with activity; increase slightly the day before the meet so she’s well hydrated on race day.
  - Drink sips consistently — don’t chug large volumes at once.
- Sodium: include dietary sodium across meals to support fluid retention and prevent cramping. Aim for a slightly higher sodium intake than usual in the 48 hours pre-meet (unless medically contraindicated).
  - Practical approach: include 1–1.5 g sodium/day (approx 2.5–4 g salt) from food plus a salty snack or 200–400 mg sodium in a sports drink per day if traveling/rehydrating after weigh-in.
  - If she completed a weigh-in earlier and had to rehydrate from a cut, use a structured rehydration plan (see below).

Meal timing & sample meal plan (48 and 24 hours out)
- Day –2 (48–24 hours before)
  - Meals: normal sized meals with higher carb portions. Examples:
    - Breakfast: oatmeal with banana, honey, and Greek yogurt. (60–80 g carbs)
    - Lunch: rice or quinoa bowl with chicken, roasted vegetables; add a bread roll. (60–80 g carbs)
    - Snack: fruit, rice cakes, or granola bar. (20–40 g carbs)
    - Dinner: pasta with lean protein (chicken/fish), simple tomato sauce; side of bread. (70–90 g carbs)
    - Evening snack (if needed): small bowl of cereal or a smoothie. (20–40 g carbs)
  - Fluids: sip water throughout day; include one sports drink (200–400 ml) during/after training or in the evening for sodium.
  - Sodium: include some salty foods (whole-food options: broth, salted nuts, salted rice cakes).

- Day –1 (24 hours before)
  - Increase carbs slightly and favor lower-fiber, familiar options to avoid GI issues:
    - Breakfast: white toast or bagel with honey and yogurt; banana. (50–70 g carbs)
    - Lunch: white rice or pasta with lean protein and cooked vegetables; avoid large raw salads. (70–100 g carbs)
    - Snack: rice cakes or low‑fiber granola bar; fruit. (20–40 g carbs)
    - Dinner: potato or sweet potato, lean protein, cooked veg; add a small bowl of simple carbs (white rice/pasta). (70–100 g carbs)
    - Evening: small carb snack if hungry (low‑fiber cereal, toast). (15–30 g carbs)
  - Fluids: continue sipping water; total ~2–2.5 L across the day. Include a salty beverage or add a little extra salt to meals.
  - Sodium: include a cup of broth or a salted snack (cracker + cheese) in the evening to ensure electrolytes are topped up.

If weigh-in and rehydration are required
- If she had to make weight and weighed in earlier, follow a staged rehydration:
  - Immediately after weigh-in: drink 500–750 ml fluid with 200–400 mg sodium and 25–50 g carbohydrate (e.g., sports drink + sandwich) in first 30–60 minutes.
  - Over the next 2–4 hours: aim to consume 1.0–1.5 L fluid with electrolytes and 1–1.5 g/kg carbs. Continue to eat familiar, slightly salty foods.
  - Avoid overdrinking water only — include electrolytes to expedite plasma volume restoration.
  - Monitor bodyweight return — aim to be near normal bodyweight 12–16 hours post weigh-in (if meet is next day).

Pre-meet day-of (Day 0) nutrition timeline
- 3–4 hours pre-lift (main pre-competition meal): 1–3 g/kg carbs, 20–30 g protein, low to moderate fat.
  - Example for 65 kg: 65–130 g carbs (this is a wide range — choose lower end if appetite or GI is a concern; many lifters do ~1–1.5 g/kg). Common practical meal: 2–3 cups white rice with chicken and a banana; or bagel with honey and yogurt.
- 90–60 minutes pre-lift: small snack 20–40 g carbs if hungry (rice cake + jam, banana).
- 30 minutes pre-lift: light carb option if needed for quick energy (10–20 g carbs) — gummy bears, sports gel, or a small piece of fruit. Sip water.
- Between attempts: 15–30 g carbs snacks if she tolerates them (gummies, rice cake piece, half a banana) and small sips of electrolyte drink. Avoid large meals between attempts.

Sodium & electrolytes on meet morning
- Include a salty breakfast or a cup of broth if she tolerates it; otherwise have a sports drink with electrolytes during warmups.
- If previously dehydrated from weight cut, supplement with 300–600 mg sodium in the 2–4 hours pre-lift (via sports drink, salted crackers, broth).
- Continue electrolytes between attempts if the meet spans many hours.

Practical food examples (easy to digest, meet-friendly)
- Carbs: white rice, white bread, bagels, potatoes, pasta, rice cakes, bananas, applesauce, low‑fiber cereal, instant oats (smaller fiber), fruit juice.
- Proteins: lean chicken/turkey, Greek yogurt, whey protein smoothie, eggs (if tolerated).
- Fluids: water, sports drinks with electrolytes, coconut water (moderate sodium), broth.
- Snacks between attempts: gummy candies, rice cakes, sports gels, small banana, pretzels (salty), energy chews.

Avoid/limit
- High‑fiber, gas‑producing foods (large raw salads, beans, cruciferous vegetables) in the 24 hours before the meet.
- Excessive fatty meals that slow gastric emptying.
- New foods, supplements, or stimulants she hasn’t used in training.
- Excessive water intake in the final 1–2 hours (can cause sloshiness or bloating) — just small sips closer to lifting.

Monitoring & adjustments
- If she typically feels bloated with higher carbs, use the lower end of the carb range and favor lower‑fiber choices.
- Track morning bodyweight vs usual to see if fluid returns after weigh-in; adjust sodium intake accordingly.
- Encourage her to practice this timing and food selection in training leading up to the meet so she knows what works.

Below is the full 3‑week meet prep program with every adjustment you requested rolled in: the original peaking structure, an inserted 5–7 day deload, 95% singles mid‑block (one for each lift), a short‑sharp heavy week after the deload, low‑fatigue competition‑prep cardio sessions, bench shoulder‑pack cue drills, and detailed meet‑morning nutrition and warmup/timing guidance. I’ve written the plan so Meet Day = Day 21. Adjust exact calendar days if your meet date differs.

Overview and principles
- Frequency: 3 gym sessions per week (Squat day, Bench day, Deadlift day) + short easy cardio sessions on recovery days. Keep sessions short and intentional.
- Objective: gradually taper volume, maintain/intact intensity exposure, reinforce bench shoulder‑pack cue with low‑volume drills, insert a deload because accumulation left her fatigued, test opener confidence with one 95% single for each lift mid‑block, then short-sharp heavy work and final taper to arrive fresh.
- Intensity cues: heavy singles 88–96% are reserved for specific days only. Avoid chasing failure. RPE for heavy singles should typically be 8–9; keep backoff/accessory work low RPE (≤7).
- Recovery priorities: sleep 8+, hydration, carbs and protein per plan, short easy cardio for circulation not fatigue, and conservative use of recovery modalities (contrast showers, light massage, foam rolling).
- Percentages refer to current recent 1RMs. If you want weights converted to kilos/pounds, give her 1RMs.

Calendar mapping (Meet Day = Day 21)
- Days 1–7: Week 1 — Peaking Week A (moderate intensity; reduced volume)
- Days 8–13: Deload Week (light technical work + restorative cardio)
- Days 12–16: 95% singles inserted at the end of deload into early short‑sharp phase (spaced for recovery) — see exact placement below
  - Recommended spacing example: Squat 95% Day 12, Bench 95% Day 14, Deadlift 95% Day 16
- Days 15–17: Short‑Sharp Week (condensed heavy/maintenance; minimal assistance)
- Days 18–21: Meet Week (light reminders, activation, cardio as described, meet on Day 21)

General session layout (for each lift day)
- Warmup: 8–12 min general (bike/walk) + mobility + progressive barbell warmups.
- Main work: 1–3 top sets depending on day (singles/doubles/triples). Heaviest singles performed only on scheduled heavy days (Week 1 heavy, Deload end 95% singles, Short‑Sharp opener-level practice).
- Assistance: minimal and targeted — keep volume low and low fatigue.
- Conditioning/cardio: easy sessions on recovery days only — 12–20 min Week 1–2, 10–15 min Week 3, RPE 1–3/10.

Detailed week-by-week plan

Week 1 — Peaking Week A (Days 1–7)
Goal: maintain heavy intensity exposure, reduce accessory volume, start freshening. Include 1 easy cardio session.

Day 1 — Squat focus (moderate heavy)
- Warmup: 8–10 min easy bike + mobility (ankles, hips); progressive empty bar sets.
- Main:
  - Back Squat: 1×5 @60%, 1×3 @70%, 1×2 @80%, 2×1 @88–92% (heavy singles; rest 3–5+ min).
  - Paused tempo sets: 2×2 @65% (technique, control).
- Assistance (reduced): Romanian DL 3×6 @60% (movement quality), Goblet or Front Squat 2×8, Core: Pallof press 3×12.
- Recovery: 10 min hip/quad rolling + mobility.
- Easy cardio (optional placement): Day after this session do 12–20 min easy bike or brisk walk (RPE 1–3/10).

Day 3 — Bench focus (moderate heavy)
- Warmup: band pull‑aparts, T‑spine mobility, empty bar x8.
- Main:
  - Bench Press (competition pause): 1×5 @60%, 1×3 @72%, 1×2 @80%, 2×1 @90–93% (singles; emphasize shoulder-pack cue).
  - Paused groove: 2×3 @70% (focus on “pull shoulders together”).
- Assistance: Close‑grip bench 3×6, DB rows 3×8/side, Triceps pushdowns 3×12.
- Mobility: posterior shoulder work and scapular drills.
- Recovery cardio: easy 12–20 min walk on a recovery day per previous instruction (not after this session if fatigued).

Day 5 — Deadlift focus (moderate heavy)
- Warmup: hip hinge drills, light cardio, progressive warmups.
- Main:
  - Deadlift: 1×5 @60%, 1×3 @72%, 1×2 @82%, 2×1 @90–92% (singles).
  - Rack pulls (just below knee): 2×3 @70% (technique).
- Assistance: Bulgarian split squat 2×8/leg, Hamstring curl 3×10, Farmer carries 3×30–50 m.
- Recovery: mobility and easy walking.

Notes Week 1:
- Keep singles technical, not max attempts to failure. Total session length ~60–75 min max.
- Add 1 easy cardio session midweek on a recovery day (12–20 min, low intensity).

Deload Week — Active recovery & neural refresh (Days 8–13)
Goal: reduce volume/intensity to restore freshness while keeping movement patterns.

Deload rules
- Volume ~30–40% of normal; intensity ~50–60% of usual loads. RPE ≤6.
- Sessions short: ~30–40 min or less. Include 2–3 easy cardio sessions (12–20 min).
- NO heavy singles >75% except we will schedule one 95% single per lift at the end of the deload window as requested — see placement below and warmup rules for those 95% singles.

Sample deload microcycle (6 days example)
Day D1 (Day 8) — Light technical lower
- Back Squat: empty bar x8; 40% x5; 55% x3 (paused emphasis). 2×6 Romanian DL @50%. 12–15 min easy bike.

Day D2 (Day 9) — Easy recovery / mobility
- 20–30 min mobility circuit + 10–15 min easy walk. Band pull‑aparts 2×20, T‑spine rotations.

Day D3 (Day 10) — Light technical upper
- Bench: empty bar x8 with shoulder-pack focus; 40% x5 paused; 55% x3 touch-and-go. Band pull‑aparts 3×15; light rows 2×8. 12–15 min easy walk.

Day D4 (Day 11) — Light lower mobility & activation

Day D5 (Day 12) — 95% Back Squat single (end of deload)

- Warmup: 8–10 min easy cardio + mobility.
- Progressive warmup sets: empty bar x8, 40% x5, 60% x3, 75% x2, 85% x1, optionally 92% x1 as confidence check; rest 4–6+ min → 1×1 @95% (single only).
- Aftercare: 5–10 min walk, light mobility; no heavy assistance. Light RDL 2×6 @50% optional.
- NOTE: If 95% feels off or causes pain, stop and replace with an opener-level single (85–90%) and prioritize recovery.

Day D6 (Day 13) — Recovery day
- 15–20 min easy walk or pool session; mobility and sleep priority.

95% Singles schedule (recommended spacing)
- Squat 95%: Day 12 (end of deload). Warmup as above.
- Bench 95%: Day 14 (two days after squat single).
- Deadlift 95%: Day 16 (two days after bench single).
Spacing rationale: 48 hours between heavy singles is minimum; if she’s still fatigued, increase spacing. These are intended as opener tests and confidence checks — not maximal training attempts. Keep only one heavy single in each session.

Short‑Sharp Week — Condensed heavy (Days 14–17)
Goal: limited heavy exposure after 95% tests, maintain specificity, minimize fatigue heading into final taper.

Day S1 (Day 14) — Bench 95% single + light assistance
- Warmup: 8–10 min cardio + mobility; progressive bench warmups (empty x8, 40% x5 paused, 60% x3 paused, 75% x2 paused, 85% x1; optional 92% x1) → 1×1 @95%.
- Aftercare: band pull‑aparts 2×20, face pulls 2×12; very light rows 2×8. Short 10–12 min easy cardio later if desired.

Day S2 (Day 15) — Light technical squat/maintenance

- Back Squat: 1–2 sets at 60–70% for groove (1×2 @60% or 2×1 at opener-level); no heavy sets.
- Mobility, light core and glute activation.
- Easy 10–15 min walk or bike session.

Day S3 (Day 16) — Deadlift 95% single
- Warmup: hip hinge work + progressive warmups (empty bar for patterning, 40% x3, 60% x2, 75% x1–2, 85% x1) → rest 4–6 min → 1×1 @95%.

Day S4 (Day 17) — Light maintenance upper or full‑body mobility
- Short bench groove work if needed (1×1 at opener or 2×2 @60%), banded upper back work, mobility and activation.
- Easy 10–12 min cardio session if desired.

Notes Short‑Sharp:
- These sessions are intentionally short. The 95% singles are mid‑block opener tests; the short‑sharp week after them is mostly maintenance and recovery.
- If any 95% single produced excessive fatigue or soreness, reduce follow-up work to mobility and rest.

Goal: absolute freshness, low-volume technical reminders, short easy cardio, and meet day prep.

- Warmup: mobility and light activation.
- Squat: 1×2 @60% or 1–2 × openers for confidence (avoid grinding).

- Deadlift: 1×1–2 @60–70% for pattern.
- Cardio: 12–15 min easy pool swim or bike (RPE 1–3).
- Focus on sleep, carbs and hydration.

Day M2 (Day 19) — Very light tune (4 days out)

Day M3 (Day 20) — Pre‑meet activation (1 day out)
- Short activation: 5–10 min light movement (bodyweight squats, banded shoulder prep, hip hinge practice). Keep under 15 min total.
- Equipment check, packing, mental rehearsal.

Day M4 — Meet Day (Day 21)

- Monitor readiness (sleep quality, resting HR, mood). If signs of excess fatigue appear, regress to mobility and rest.
- Avoid new supplements, heavy massage <48 hours pre-meet if it causes soreness.

- Morning meal 2.5–3 hours pre-lift: 40–70 g carbs typical (bagel + honey + yogurt, or rice + chicken + banana) and 20–30 g protein.

  - General warmup: 5–8 min easy bike/walk and mobility.
  - Barbell warmups: incremental jumps to opener (see squat/bench/deadlift warmup examples below).
  - Emphasize bench shoulder‑pack cue during every warmup rep.

- Between attempts: eat 15–30 g carbs snacks (gummies, rice cake, half banana), sip electrolytes, and do breathing/visualization and short mobility to avoid stiffness.

Example warmup progressions for each lift (adjust to her numbers)
- Squat: empty bar x5–8, 40% x3, 60% x2, 75% x1–2, 85% x1 (confidence), opener weight single. Last heavy warmup 3–6 min before platform.

Below is the full 3‑week meet prep program with every adjustment you requested rolled in: the original peaking structure, an inserted 5–7 day deload, 95% singles mid‑block (one for each lift), a short‑sharp heavy week after the deload, low‑fatigue competition‑prep cardio sessions, bench shoulder‑pack cue drills, and detailed meet‑morning nutrition and warmup/timing guidance. I’ve written the plan so Meet Day = Day 21. Adjust exact calendar days if your meet date differs.

Overview and principles
- Frequency: 3 gym sessions per week (Squat day, Bench day, Deadlift day) + short easy cardio sessions on recovery days. Keep sessions short and intentional.
- Objective: gradually taper volume, maintain/intact intensity exposure, reinforce bench shoulder‑pack cue with low‑volume drills, insert a deload because accumulation left her fatigued, test opener confidence with one 95% single for each lift mid‑block, then short-sharp heavy work and final taper to arrive fresh.
- Intensity cues: heavy singles 88–96% are reserved for specific days only. Avoid chasing failure. RPE for heavy singles should typically be 8–9; keep backoff/accessory work low RPE (≤7).
- Recovery priorities: sleep 8+, hydration, carbs and protein per plan, short easy cardio for circulation not fatigue, and conservative use of recovery modalities (contrast showers, light massage, foam rolling).
- Percentages refer to current recent 1RMs. If you want weights converted to kilos/pounds, give her 1RMs.

Calendar mapping (Meet Day = Day 21)
- Days 1–7: Week 1 — Peaking Week A (moderate intensity; reduced volume)
- Days 8–13: Deload Week (light technical work + restorative cardio)
- Days 12–16: 95% singles inserted at the end of deload into early short‑sharp phase (spaced for recovery) — see exact placement below
  - Recommended spacing example: Squat 95% Day 12, Bench 95% Day 14, Deadlift 95% Day 16
- Days 15–17: Short‑Sharp Week (condensed heavy/maintenance; minimal assistance)
- Days 18–21: Meet Week (light reminders, activation, cardio as described, meet on Day 21)

General session layout (for each lift day)
- Warmup: 8–12 min general (bike/walk) + mobility + progressive barbell warmups.
- Main work: 1–3 top sets depending on day (singles/doubles/triples). Heaviest singles performed only on scheduled heavy days (Week 1 heavy, Deload end 95% singles, Short‑Sharp opener-level practice).
- Assistance: minimal and targeted — keep volume low and low fatigue.
- Conditioning/cardio: easy sessions on recovery days only — 12–20 min Week 1–2, 10–15 min Week 3, RPE 1–3/10.

Detailed week-by-week plan

Week 1 — Peaking Week A (Days 1–7)
Goal: maintain heavy intensity exposure, reduce accessory volume, start freshening. Include 1 easy cardio session.

Day 1 — Squat focus (moderate heavy)
- Warmup: 8–10 min easy bike + mobility (ankles, hips); progressive empty bar sets.
- Main:
  - Back Squat: 1×5 @60%, 1×3 @70%, 1×2 @80%, 2×1 @88–92% (heavy singles; rest 3–5+ min).
  - Paused tempo sets: 2×2 @65% (technique, control).
- Assistance (reduced): Romanian DL 3×6 @60% (movement quality), Goblet or Front Squat 2×8, Core: Pallof press 3×12.
- Recovery: 10 min hip/quad rolling + mobility.
- Easy cardio (optional placement): Day after this session do 12–20 min easy bike or brisk walk (RPE 1–3/10).

Day 3 — Bench focus (moderate heavy)
- Warmup: band pull‑aparts, T‑spine mobility, empty bar x8.
- Main:
  - Bench Press (competition pause): 1×5 @60%, 1×3 @72%, 1×2 @80%, 2×1 @90–93% (singles; emphasize shoulder-pack cue).
  - Paused groove: 2×3 @70% (focus on “pull shoulders together”).
- Assistance: Close‑grip bench 3×6, DB rows 3×8/side, Triceps pushdowns 3×12.
- Mobility: posterior shoulder work and scapular drills.
- Recovery cardio: easy 12–20 min walk on a recovery day per previous instruction (not after this session if fatigued).

Day 5 — Deadlift focus (moderate heavy)
- Warmup: hip hinge drills, light cardio, progressive warmups.
- Main:
  - Deadlift: 1×5 @60%, 1×3 @72%, 1×2 @82%, 2×1 @90–92% (singles).
  - Rack pulls (just below knee): 2×3 @70% (technique).
- Assistance: Bulgarian split squat 2×8/leg, Hamstring curl 3×10, Farmer carries 3×30–50 m.
- Recovery: mobility and easy walking.

Notes Week 1:
- Keep singles technical, not max attempts to failure. Total session length ~60–75 min max.
- Add 1 easy cardio session midweek on a recovery day (12–20 min, low intensity).

Deload Week — Active recovery & neural refresh (Days 8–13)
Goal: reduce volume/intensity to restore freshness while keeping movement patterns.

Deload rules
- Volume ~30–40% of normal; intensity ~50–60% of usual loads. RPE ≤6.
- Sessions short: ~30–40 min or less. Include 2–3 easy cardio sessions (12–20 min).
- NO heavy singles >75% except we will schedule one 95% single per lift at the end of the deload window as requested — see placement below and warmup rules for those 95% singles.

Sample deload microcycle (6 days example)
Day D1 (Day 8) — Light technical lower
- Back Squat: empty bar x8; 40% x5; 55% x3 (paused emphasis). 2×6 Romanian DL @50%. 12–15 min easy bike.

Day D2 (Day 9) — Easy recovery / mobility
- 20–30 min mobility circuit + 10–15 min easy walk. Band pull‑aparts 2×20, T‑spine rotations.

Day D3 (Day 10) — Light technical upper
- Bench: empty bar x8 with shoulder-pack focus; 40% x5 paused; 55% x3 touch-and-go. Band pull‑aparts 3×15; light rows 2×8. 12–15 min easy walk.

Day D4 (Day 11) — Light lower mobility & activation
- Bodyweight split squats 2×8; glute bridges 2×10; light carries 2×30 m; 12–20 min easy bike or pool swim.

Day D5 (Day 12) — 95% Back Squat single (end of deload)
- This is the first of the three requested 95% singles (Squat).
- Warmup: 8–10 min easy cardio + mobility.
- Progressive warmup sets: empty bar x8, 40% x5, 60% x3, 75% x2, 85% x1, optionally 92% x1 as confidence check; rest 4–6+ min → 1×1 @95% (single only).
- Aftercare: 5–10 min walk, light mobility; no heavy assistance. Light RDL 2×6 @50% optional.
- NOTE: If 95% feels off or causes pain, stop and replace with an opener-level single (85–90%) and prioritize recovery.

Day D6 (Day 13) — Recovery day
- 15–20 min easy walk or pool session; mobility and sleep priority.

95% Singles schedule (recommended spacing)
- Squat 95%: Day 12 (end of deload). Warmup as above.
- Bench 95%: Day 14 (two days after squat single).
- Deadlift 95%: Day 16 (two days after bench single).
Spacing rationale: 48 hours between heavy singles is minimum; if she’s still fatigued, increase spacing. These are intended as opener tests and confidence checks — not maximal training attempts. Keep only one heavy single in each session.

Short‑Sharp Week — Condensed heavy (Days 14–17)
Goal: limited heavy exposure after 95% tests, maintain specificity, minimize fatigue heading into final taper.

Day S1 (Day 14) — Bench 95% single + light assistance
- Warmup: 8–10 min cardio + mobility; progressive bench warmups (empty x8, 40% x5 paused, 60% x3 paused, 75% x2 paused, 85% x1; optional 92% x1) → 1×1 @95%.
- Aftercare: band pull‑aparts 2×20, face pulls 2×12; very light rows 2×8. Short 10–12 min easy cardio later if desired.

Day S2 (Day 15) — Light technical squat/maintenance
- Keep this session short and low volume because squat 95% was Day 12.
- Back Squat: 1–2 sets at 60–70% for groove (1×2 @60% or 2×1 at opener-level); no heavy sets.
- Mobility, light core and glute activation.
- Easy 10–15 min walk or bike session.

Day S3 (Day 16) — Deadlift 95% single
- Warmup: hip hinge work + progressive warmups (empty bar for patterning, 40% x3, 60% x2, 75% x1–2, 85% x1) → rest 4–6 min → 1×1 @95%.
- Aftercare: 5–10 min walk, light reverse hypers or glute ham raises 2×6 @low load. No heavy assistance.

Day S4 (Day 17) — Light maintenance upper or full‑body mobility
- Short bench groove work if needed (1×1 at opener or 2×2 @60%), banded upper back work, mobility and activation.
- Easy 10–12 min cardio session if desired.

Notes Short‑Sharp:
- These sessions are intentionally short. The 95% singles are mid‑block opener tests; the short‑sharp week after them is mostly maintenance and recovery.
- If any 95% single produced excessive fatigue or soreness, reduce follow-up work to mobility and rest.

Meet Week — Taper & competition prep (Days 18–21)
Goal: absolute freshness, low-volume technical reminders, short easy cardio, and meet day prep.

Day M1 (Day 18) — Light technical full‑body (7 days out)
- Warmup: mobility and light activation.
- Squat: 1×2 @60% or 1–2 × openers for confidence (avoid grinding).
- Bench: 1×2 @60% with pronounced shoulder-pack and 1–2 paused opener-level singles if desired.
- Deadlift: 1×1–2 @60–70% for pattern.
- Cardio: 12–15 min easy pool swim or bike (RPE 1–3).
- Focus on sleep, carbs and hydration.

Day M2 (Day 19) — Very light tune (4 days out)
- Optional short session: 10–12 min brisk walk or easy bike early in the day, plus mobility and band pull‑aparts. No barbell work necessary unless she wants 1 opener-level touch single only.

Day M3 (Day 20) — Pre‑meet activation (1 day out)
- Short activation: 5–10 min light movement (bodyweight squats, banded shoulder prep, hip hinge practice). Keep under 15 min total.
- Equipment check, packing, mental rehearsal.

Day M4 — Meet Day (Day 21)
- Follow full meet warmup and attempt plan (detailed below under Meet-morning & Warmup).
- Nutrition and hydration per the 48‑hour plan and meet-day guidance.

Competition-Prep Cardio (all weeks)
- Week 1: 1 session 12–20 min easy (day after heavy session). Week 2 (deload): 2–3 easy sessions 12–20 min for circulation. Week 3: 2 short easy sessions 10–15 min (Day 18 and Day 19), plus a 5–10 min activation Day 20 if desired.
- Modes: brisk walk, easy bike, pool swim. Always low intensity (RPE 1–3/10) and not fatiguing.

Bench shoulder‑pack cue reinforcement
- Keep the cue “pull shoulders together” throughout the peaking block.
- Low-volume drills to include regularly:
  - Band scapular retractions: 2×10–15 (warmups).
  - Paused bench groove: 1–2 sets of 2–3 reps at 60–70% focusing on cue (Weeks 1 and deload). In Short‑Sharp and Meet Week use only opener-level singles with the cue.
  - Isometric holds at chest: 2–3 sets of 3–5 s @50–60% in warmups if needed.
  - Video one warmup single in the 95% bench session to check position; make only micro adjustments.

Recovery & monitoring throughout
- Sleep 8+ hours; naps if possible.
- Monitor readiness (sleep quality, resting HR, mood). If signs of excess fatigue appear, regress to mobility and rest.
- Avoid new supplements, heavy massage <48 hours pre-meet if it causes soreness.

48‑Hour Pre‑Meet Nutrition & Hydration (Days –2 and –1) — integrated into plan
- Carbs: aim for ~4–6 g/kg/day on Day –2 and Day –1 (adjust to bodyweight). For a 65 kg client: ~260–390 g carbs/day. Favor lower-fiber, familiar carbs on Day –1.
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day.
- Fat: moderate but keep meals easy to digest near the meet.
- Fluids: baseline ~30–40 ml/kg/day (≈1.8–2.6 L for 60–65 kg), slightly increase Day –1; sip consistently.
- Sodium: slightly elevated intake Day –2 and Day –1 — include salty meals/snacks and/or a cup of broth. Rough practical target: include a few grams of salt across meals (2.5–4 g salt/day) or a sports drink with electrolytes.
- If weigh-in/re-hydration needed: follow staged rehydration (immediately after weigh-in drink 500–750 ml with sodium and 25–50 g carbs; then 1–1.5 L and 1–1.5 g/kg carbs over next 2–4 hours).
- Day 0 (meet morning): main meal 3–4 hours pre-lift with ~1–1.5 g/kg carbs (adjust appetite), 20–30 g protein. Small snacks 60–90 and 15–30 minutes pre-lift (10–30 g carbs). Sip electrolyte drink through warmups.

Meet‑morning warmup & timing (full procedure)
- Wake ~2.5–4 hours before platform attempts; drink 300–500 ml water on waking.
- Morning meal 2.5–3 hours pre-lift: 40–70 g carbs typical (bagel + honey + yogurt, or rice + chicken + banana) and 20–30 g protein.
- 90–60 min pre-lift: small carb snack if desired (rice cake, banana).
- Arrive at venue early; begin progressive warmups ~25–40 min before platform call for her flight:
  - General warmup: 5–8 min easy bike/walk and mobility.
  - Barbell warmups: incremental jumps to opener (see squat/bench/deadlift warmup examples below).
  - Emphasize bench shoulder‑pack cue during every warmup rep.
- Final warmup single 3–6 min before platform opener. If long delays occur, use short re‑activation singles with light loads (empty bar or 40–60%) rather than extended warmups.
- Between attempts: eat 15–30 g carbs snacks (gummies, rice cake, half banana), sip electrolytes, and do breathing/visualization and short mobility to avoid stiffness.

Example warmup progressions for each lift (adjust to her numbers)
- Squat: empty bar x5–8, 40% x3, 60% x2, 75% x1–2, 85% x1 (confidence), opener weight single. Last heavy warmup 3–6 min before platform.
- Bench: empty bar x8 (focus shoulders), 40% x5 paused, 60% x3 paused, 75% x2 paused, 85% x1 paused (optional), opener single with full pause. Keep the shoulder-pack cue.
- Deadlift: empty bar patterning x3–6 (hip hinge patterns), 40% x3, 60% x2, 75% x1–2, opener single.

Attempt selection guidance (use 95% singles feedback)
- Use the 95% single results to set openers:
  - If 95% single felt confident and fast: opener around 88–92% is reasonable (very likely successful).
  - If 95% felt heavy but successful: choose a conservative opener (~85–90%) to secure three lifts.
  - If 95% felt off or incomplete: choose a reliable conservative opener (~82–88%) and rely on feel in warmups for second attempt.
- Typical strategy: Opener = a lift she can hit for a solid single in training (high success probability), Second = ~95–99% (challenging), Third = PR attempt depending on meet goals.

Post‑95% single recovery guidance
- After each 95% single: prioritize sleep, carbs (50–100 g in next 24 hrs), protein intake, light mobility, and gentle circulation work (short walks, light pool swim).
- Consider light contrast showers or gentle massage if that helps recovery, but avoid deep tissue work that causes soreness.

Contingencies & coaching notes
- If any of the 95% singles causes pain or leaves her excessively fatigued, stop further heavy attempts and revert to opener-level practice and rest.
- Keep verbal cues consistent and limited; for bench use the same cue wording she’s practiced — “pull shoulders together” — across warmups and attempts.
- Do not introduce new technical cues in Week 3. Use video only for small refinements between Week 2 and Short‑Sharp if necessary.
